criteria.text: The participant has a pathologically confirmed malignancy for which high-dose rate brachytherapy is appropriate as a component of their therapeutic regimen.
The participant is greater than 18 years of age.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0, 1, or 2.

The participant has a primary medical or surgical oncologist in the community or at National Cancer Institute (NCI) who is willing to collaborate with the Radiation Oncology Branch (ROB) staff in the clinical management of the participant.

The participant is of childbearing or child-fathering potential and is willing to use a medically acceptable form of birth control, which includes abstinence, while they are being treated on this study.
The participant has endometrial cancer.

The participant is at a higher risk of recurrence (because of either grade, myometrial invasion, lymphatic vascular space invasion, tumor size, lymph node status, tumor extension, presence or absence of surgical staging).
The participant has suffered a recurrence at the vaginal cuff.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary endometrial cancer.
The participant has cervical cancer.
The participant is unable to undergo surgery and must have treatment for an inoperable primary cervical cancer.

The participant has locally advanced cervical cancer in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation either in a palliative or curative setting (definitive or post-operative setting).
The participant has lung cancer.
The participant has an endobronchial component causing symptoms.
The participant cannot undergo resection because of poor lung function or distant lung metastasis.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant has infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS), stage T0, T1, and T2 less than or equal to 3.0 cm, N0 and M0.
The participant is benefiting from high dose radiation (HDR) as either as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation regimen.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has localized prostate cancer (T1b-T3b) in whom brachytherapy will be integrated as a boost to external beam radiation or used as monotherapy for definitive management.
The participant is cognitively impaired and cannot give informed consent.
The participant is currently receiving concurrent investigational chemotherapeutic agents.

The participant is receiving concomitant chemotherapy administration in the 5 days preceding brachytherapy (except for gynecological cancer patients who may have received concurrent chemotherapy as a component of their treatment regimen).
The participant is pregnant or breast-feeding.

The participant has a clinically significant unrelated systemic illness (serious infections or significant cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic or other organ dysfunction), which in the judgment of the Principal or Associate Investigator would compromise the participant s ability to tolerate this therapy or are likely to interfere with the study procedures or results.
The participant is deemed unable or unlikely to adhere to protocol treatment.
The participant has abnormal bleeding times or active anti-coagulation therapy.
The participant has platelets less than 100,000 per mm(3).
The participant has Prothrombin time (PT)/Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) greater than 1.5 the upper normal limit (UNL).

The participant or tumor/anatomical factors may prevent brachytherapy apparatus from being properly and safely inserted and positioned and from radiation therapy being administered per American Brachytherapy Society (ABS) guidelines.
The participant has breast cancer.
The participant is inappropriate for standard breast conservation therapy (Multicentric disease, inability to achieve clear margins).
The participant is a male with breast cancer.
The participant has autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Scleroderma, etc.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has prostate cancer.
The participant has distant metastases.
The participant has lymph node metastases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of Patients Receiving High-Dose Rate Brachytherapy". I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with a cancer for which high-dose rate brachytherapy (a type of internal radiation therapy) is considered an appropriate part of your treatment plan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if that's appropriate for me. My cancer is serous carcinoma of the endometrium, and I've had a hysterectomy, but I'm not sure if brachytherapy is part of the plan for my current situation with liver lesions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “The participant is greater than 18 years of age.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 65 years old, so I am definitely greater than 18.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your ECOG performance status? It's a score from 0 to 2 that measures how well you can do usual daily activities. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My ECOG performance status is 1. I am restricted in physically strenuous activity but I am ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a primary medical or surgical oncologist (in the community or at NCI) who is willing to work with the study's Radiation Oncology team to manage your care?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a specific oncologist willing to work with their Radiation Oncology team. I have been seeing doctors for my chemotherapy and surgeries, but I haven't discussed this trial arrangement with them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently of childbearing or child-fathering potential (meaning you could potentially become pregnant or father a child)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am 65 years old, so I am not of childbearing potential.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your pathology or surgical reports, do you know if you have any higher-risk features for recurrence, such as tumor grade, size, or spread to lymph nodes?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about tumor grade or size, but my pathology report did show spread to the lymph nodes, specifically the right and left external iliac nodes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a recurrence of cancer at the vaginal cuff?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a recurrence at the vaginal cuff. My recent scans show progression in the liver and lymph nodes, but I haven't been told about any issues at the cuff.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that you are unable to undergo surgery for your endometrial cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I am unable to undergo surgery. I had a hysterectomy in the past, but I am not sure about my current surgical eligibility for this trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, have you been diagnosed with cervical cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with cervical cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that you are unable to undergo surgery for your cervical cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I am unable to undergo surgery for cervical cancer, because I don't have cervical cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with lung cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with cancer in your lung that is causing symptoms?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have cancer in my lung causing symptoms. My scans show progression in the liver and lymph nodes, but I haven't been told about any issues in my lungs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by your doctor that you cannot undergo surgery for your cancer because of poor lung function or distant lung metastasis?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have poor lung function or distant lung metastasis. My scans show progression in the liver and lymph nodes, but I haven't been told about issues in my lungs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with breast cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with breast cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with infiltrating ductal carcinoma or ductal carcinoma in-situ (DCIS) of the breast?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with breast cancer or any type of ductal carcinoma. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently receiving high-dose radiation (HDR) as a boost or accelerated partial breast irradiation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not currently receiving high-dose radiation. I was taken off treatment for progression on imaging in October 2022.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with prostate cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with prostate cancer. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any memory or thinking problems that make it hard for you to understand study information and give consent?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have memory or thinking problems. I am able to understand information and give consent.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking any investigational chemotherapy drugs as part of another study or trial?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not currently taking any investigational chemotherapy drugs. I was taken off my previous treatment for progression in October 2022 and am not in another trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any chemotherapy in the 5 days before your brachytherapy treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't received chemotherapy in the last 5 days. I was taken off treatment for progression on imaging in October 2022.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breast-feeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am 65 years old, so I am not pregnant or breast-feeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any serious ongoing health issues, such as significant heart, lung, liver, or kidney problems, or serious infections, that might make it hard to tolerate this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have some serious health issues. I have liver lesions from cancer progression, and I recently had high fevers with chills. I also have worsening fatigue and peripheral neuropathy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand your current health, are you currently experiencing any active infections (like the fevers you mentioned) or do you have significant liver, heart, or lung problems that might make it hard to tolerate this treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have had fevers and chills recently, which suggests an infection, and I have liver lesions from cancer progression. I am not sure if this counts as a significant liver problem for the trial, but I do have these active issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand your situation, do you feel you would be able to follow the treatment schedule and instructions as planned, or are there any reasons you might find it difficult to adhere to the protocol?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I think I can follow the schedule, as I am ambulatory and able to carry out light work. However, my worsening fatigue and recent high fevers might make it difficult.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Given your fatigue and recent fevers, do you think you will be able to attend all scheduled treatment visits and follow the instructions exactly as planned, or is there a significant chance you might miss appointments or struggle with the regimen?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I will be able to attend all visits or follow the regimen exactly. My worsening fatigue and recent high fevers make it difficult to know if I can stick to the schedule.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check one more safety detail, are you currently taking any blood thinners (anti-coagulation therapy), or have you had any recent issues with abnormal bleeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I am currently taking blood thinners. My medication list includes propranolol and others, but I don't see any anticoagulants listed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by a doctor that your anatomy or tumor location might make it difficult to safely insert the brachytherapy device or deliver the radiation treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my anatomy or tumor location makes it difficult. My scans show progression in the liver and lymph nodes, but I haven't been told about issues with the anatomy for brachytherapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by your doctor that your breast cancer is in multiple separate areas (multicentric) or that it might be hard to remove all of it with clear edges (clear margins)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have breast cancer, so this question doesn't apply to me. My diagnosis is serous carcinoma of the endometrium.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any autoimmune disorders, such as lupus (SLE) or scleroderma? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have an autoimmune disorder like lupus or scleroderma. My medical history lists hypertension, hiatal hernia, high cholesterol, hypothyroidism, osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis, but nothing about autoimmune diseases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
